chapter_summary: Proverbs 12 continues Solomon's great gallery of contrasts, holding the righteous and the wicked side by side in every verse. The chapter sweeps across a wide range of life: how we learn, how we speak, how we work, how we treat animals, how we handle anger, and what our words do to others. Truth is shown to be permanent; lies, fleeting. Hard work is shown to yield honour; laziness, poverty. Kindness in speech is healing; cruelty is like a sword. The chapter closes with a magnificent promise: the path of righteousness leads to life — and on that path, there is no death.
main_lesson: God rewards honesty, hard work, and kind words. Lying, laziness, and cruel words bring trouble.

memory_verse.kjv: In the way of righteousness is life; and in the pathway thereof there is no death.
memory_verse.little_bible: Walking God's right way leads to life. On that path, there is no death!

parent_guide:
Proverbs 12 is an ideal chapter for children because almost every verse connects to daily life — the way we talk, the way we work, the way we respond to being corrected, and the way we treat the vulnerable. The antithetical structure (righteous vs. wicked, truth vs. lies, diligent vs. lazy) helps children understand morality not in abstract terms but through vivid contrasts.

Verses 1 and 15 together make a powerful pair for teaching children about correction: loving instruction and listening to counsel are marks of wisdom, while refusing to be taught and being right in one's own eyes are marks of foolishness. This is a gentle but firm message for children who resist parental guidance.

Verses 17-22 on truthfulness and lying deserve special attention. The chapter teaches that lying lips are an abomination to God — the strongest language of divine aversion. Children need to understand that honesty is not just a social nicety but a matter of God's holiness and delight. Use these verses to build a family culture where truth is treasured.

Verse 28 makes an excellent closing devotion. Righteousness is not just a rule to follow — it is a path that leads to life. Help your children understand that obedience to God is the road to flourishing, both now and forever.
application_for_children: This week, practise being a truth-teller in every situation. When you are tempted to lie or shade the truth, remember: God delights in honest lips. Speak truth and walk the path that leads to life.

verses.kjv: Whoso loveth instruction loveth knowledge: but he that hateth reproof is brutish.
verses.little_bible: If you love being taught, you love knowledge. Hating correction is foolish. Only animals never learn from correction.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Love learning and you love knowledge.
verses.meaning: Embracing correction and instruction is the mark of a person who genuinely pursues wisdom. Refusing correction — hating reproof — is described in the strongest terms: it is 'brutish,' the behaviour of an unthinking animal rather than a wise human being made in God's image.
verses.prayer: God, help me love being taught and corrected.
verses.discussion_question: How do you feel when someone corrects you? Why?
verses.family_discussion: How can we create a family culture where receiving correction is seen as a gift rather than an attack — where reproof strengthens rather than shames?
verses.do_it_today: The next time someone corrects you today, say 'thank you' and really mean it. Think about what you can learn from it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A smiling child eagerly listening to a teacher pointing at a book, warm golden classroom light, gentle watercolour style

verses.kjv: A good man obtaineth favour of the LORD: but a man of wicked devices will he condemn.
verses.little_bible: God shows favour to the good person. But the person who plans wicked things — God will judge them.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Good people receive God's favour.
verses.meaning: Goodness and wickedness are not morally equal before God. The good person — one who genuinely pursues righteousness — receives divine favour. The person who schemes and devises wicked plans will face God's condemnation. God is not a neutral observer of human conduct.
verses.prayer: God, help me be truly good, not just look good.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to have God's favour on your life?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help children pursue goodness that comes from the heart — not just outward behaviour performed for approval?
verses.do_it_today: Do one genuinely good thing today with no one watching and no reward expected — just because goodness pleases God.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child with a warm glow of golden light around them as they help someone, representing God's favour, gentle watercolour scene

verses.kjv: A man shall not be established by wickedness: but the root of the righteous shall not be moved.
verses.little_bible: Doing wrong can never build a lasting life. But the righteous person is like a tree with deep roots — they cannot be blown over.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Righteousness gives deep, unshakeable roots.
verses.meaning: Wickedness cannot provide a stable foundation for life — it may appear to prosper but will always collapse. Righteousness, by contrast, is like a deep root system: it provides stability that cannot be uprooted by any storm.
verses.prayer: God, make me rooted in righteousness and unmoveable.
verses.discussion_question: What makes a tree hard to blow over in a big storm?
verses.family_discussion: What are the spiritual 'roots' we are developing in our family — habits, rhythms, and convictions that will hold our children firm in difficult seasons?
verses.do_it_today: Draw a tree today. Label the roots with righteous things you want to grow in — honesty, kindness, obedience to God.
verses.illustration_prompt: A strong tree with deep visible roots standing firm in a storm while a shallow-rooted tree topples over, warm earthy watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: A virtuous woman is a crown to her husband: but she that maketh ashamed is as rottenness in his bones.
verses.little_bible: A woman of good character is like a crown on her husband's head — she honours him. But a woman who brings shame is like a sickness that rots from the inside.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A good woman is a crown to her husband.
verses.meaning: A woman of virtue — moral integrity, strength, and faithfulness — brings honour and dignity to her husband. The contrast is stark: shameful behaviour does not just embarrass but destroys from within, like a disease in the bones.
verses.prayer: God, help me be someone who honours those I love.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to be a crown to your family?
verses.family_discussion: How do we build a family where every member — husband, wife, child — sees themselves as called to honour and strengthen the others rather than shame them?
verses.do_it_today: Say one genuine, honouring thing about a family member to someone else today — speak well of those you love.
verses.illustration_prompt: A woman wearing a radiant crown standing beside her husband, both smiling with dignity and warmth, soft watercolour portrait

verses.kjv: The thoughts of the righteous are right: but the counsels of the wicked are deceit.
verses.little_bible: The righteous person thinks right thoughts. The wicked person's plans are built on deceit and lies.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Righteous people think right thoughts.
verses.meaning: The inner life — what we think and plan — reveals our true character. Righteous thoughts lead to just actions; wicked counsel is grounded in deception. What we nurture in our minds shapes what we do in the world.
verses.prayer: God, guard my thoughts and keep them right.
verses.discussion_question: Did you know God sees your thoughts too?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help children guard their thought life — understanding that inner purity matters as much as outward behaviour?
verses.do_it_today: When a wrong or unkind thought comes today, practise replacing it with a good one. Tell God what you are thinking and ask for His help.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child with a glowing, pure heart visible through their chest, surrounded by good and loving thoughts as gentle light, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: The words of the wicked are to lie in wait for blood: but the mouth of the upright shall deliver them.
verses.little_bible: The wicked use words like traps — to harm people. But the upright person's words can rescue those who are in danger.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Upright words rescue. Wicked words trap.
verses.meaning: Words are powerful weapons — for good or for evil. The wicked use speech as a trap, an ambush for harm. The upright person uses speech as a tool of rescue and deliverance. Every word we speak either tears down or builds up, harms or saves.
verses.prayer: God, let my words rescue people, not trap them.
verses.discussion_question: Can words really hurt people or save them? How?
verses.family_discussion: Can you think of a time when the right words at the right moment made a real difference — perhaps even saved someone from harm or despair?
verses.do_it_today: Look for someone today who seems sad or in trouble. Speak one encouraging, rescuing word to them.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child speaking kind words that appear as a rope pulling a friend out of a pit, versus a shadowy figure setting a word-trap, watercolour contrast illustration

verses.kjv: The wicked are overthrown, and are not: but the house of the righteous shall stand.
verses.little_bible: The wicked are knocked down and gone. But the righteous person's house stands firm.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The righteous person's house stands firm.
verses.meaning: Wickedness leads to ultimate collapse and erasure — the wicked 'are not,' as if swept away entirely. But righteousness builds a lasting house — a legacy, a family, a life that endures.
verses.prayer: God, build my life on righteousness that will stand.
verses.discussion_question: What makes a house strong enough to stand in a storm?
verses.family_discussion: What are we building in our family right now — what foundations are we laying that will allow our home to stand long after we are gone?
verses.do_it_today: Look around your home today. Name one spiritual value this house stands on. Write it on a piece of paper and place it somewhere visible.
verses.illustration_prompt: A strong bright house standing on solid rock while dark storm clouds swirl, a righteous family inside, warm watercolour scene

verses.kjv: A man is commended according to his wisdom: but he that is of a perverse heart shall be despised.
verses.little_bible: People praise a person for their wisdom. But someone with a twisted, dishonest heart will be looked down on.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wisdom earns true praise from others.
verses.meaning: True commendation — lasting respect from others — comes from genuine wisdom. A perverse heart, however, inevitably leads to contempt. Character, not performance, determines how we are ultimately regarded.
verses.prayer: God, make me wise from the inside out.
verses.discussion_question: What is one thing you admire about a truly wise person you know?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children pursue inner wisdom rather than external approval — building character that will be genuinely admired?
verses.do_it_today: Think of the wisest person you know. Write down one thing they do that you can try to copy this week.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child being commended by elders, surrounded by warm respectful faces, wisdom shown as a gentle glow around them, soft watercolour scene

verses.kjv: He that is despised, and hath a servant, is better than he that honoureth himself, and lacketh bread.
verses.little_bible: Being humble with food is better than boasting. Boasting and going hungry is foolish. True contentment beats empty pride.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Humble and fed is better than proud and hungry.
verses.meaning: This proverb punctures self-promotion. The person who is modest but has real provision is better off than the one who exalts himself but lacks the basics of life. Genuine provision beats impressive-sounding boasting.
verses.prayer: God, keep me humble and truly provided for.
verses.discussion_question: What is the difference between pride and real success?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate genuine contentment and humility in our children — teaching them to value what is real over what impresses others?
verses.do_it_today: Choose one area where you have been showing off. Try doing the same thing quietly today — no one needs to know.
verses.illustration_prompt: A cheerful humble child eating a simple meal contrasted with a boastful child surrounded by empty dishes, gentle warm watercolour comparison

verses.kjv: A righteous man regardeth the life of his animal: but the tender mercies of the wicked are cruel.
verses.little_bible: A righteous person takes good care of their animals. Even the kindest thing a wicked person does is still cruel.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Good people are kind even to their animals.
verses.meaning: Care for animals is a window into moral character. The righteous person's compassion extends even to those who cannot speak for themselves. The wicked, by contrast, are so corrupted that even their acts of mercy are cruel — wickedness distorts everything it touches.
verses.prayer: God, make me kind to every living thing You made.
verses.discussion_question: Why do you think God cares how we treat animals?
verses.family_discussion: Compassion toward animals is a training ground for compassion toward people. How are we cultivating a habit of gentleness toward all living things in our home?
verses.do_it_today: If you have a pet, give it extra care today. If you see any animal, be gentle. Let kindness become a habit.
verses.illustration_prompt: A smiling child gently feeding a small animal, caring and tender, soft green and golden watercolour outdoor scene

verses.kjv: He that tilleth his land shall be satisfied with bread: but he that followeth vain persons is void of understanding.
verses.little_bible: The person who works their land will have plenty to eat. But following empty, foolish people leads nowhere.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Work hard and you will have enough.
verses.meaning: Diligent work — faithful attention to one's responsibilities — produces satisfaction and provision. Following after vain or empty people is the opposite: it leads to emptiness. The company we keep and the use of our time shape our harvest.
verses.prayer: God, help me work hard and follow wise people.
verses.discussion_question: Do you choose friends who encourage you to work hard or be lazy?
verses.family_discussion: What kinds of influences — friends, media, activities — are pulling our children toward diligence, and which are pulling them toward emptiness?
verses.do_it_today: Do one chore or task today that you normally avoid. Finish it completely. Notice how it feels to have done the work.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child digging and tending a garden with a full harvest of vegetables nearby, warm earthy colours, cheerful watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The wicked desireth the net of evil men: but the root of the righteous yieldeth fruit.
verses.little_bible: Wicked people want to take what others have — like a trap. But the righteous person grows fruit from their own roots.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The righteous grow their own good fruit.
verses.meaning: The wicked desire to seize what belongs to others — to capture gain through evil means. But the righteous do not need to steal or trap: their own roots naturally yield fruit. Righteousness is productive from the inside.
verses.prayer: God, help me grow fruit by staying rooted in You.
verses.discussion_question: How does a tree grow fruit — by grabbing it or by staying rooted?
verses.family_discussion: How are we helping our children grow genuine spiritual fruit through healthy roots — time in God's Word, prayer, and good community?
verses.do_it_today: Name one good 'fruit' you want in your life — like patience or kindness. Ask God to grow it in you from the inside.
verses.illustration_prompt: A fruitful tree with deep roots beside a barren trap on the ground, lush green and golden watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The wicked is snared by the transgression of his lips: but the just shall come out of trouble.
verses.little_bible: The wicked person gets caught in their own wrong words — like a trap. But the just person comes out of trouble safely.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wrong words trap the wicked. The just escape.
verses.meaning: There is a terrible irony in wickedness: the very words the wicked use to harm others become the trap that catches them. The just person, however, finds a way through trouble rather than being destroyed by it.
verses.prayer: God, guard my lips from words that trap me.
verses.discussion_question: Have wrong words ever gotten you into trouble?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help children understand that words have consequences — and that careless or dishonest speech creates real and lasting problems?
verses.do_it_today: Before you speak today, take one breath and ask: 'Will this word help or hurt?' Make a habit of it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A figure caught in a word-trap of their own making, tangled in a net of spoken words, while a just figure walks free through an open path, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: A man shall be satisfied with good by the fruit of his mouth: and the recompence of a man's hands shall be rendered unto him.
verses.little_bible: Good words bring good things back to you. Your hard work comes back to you as a reward. What you put out comes back.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Good words and work bring good rewards.
verses.meaning: There is a beautiful reciprocity in life under God's ordering: the good we speak and the good we do return to us as blessing. This is not karma but God's moral order — faithfulness and goodness are not wasted.
verses.prayer: God, let my words and work bear good fruit.
verses.discussion_question: Have good words or hard work ever been rewarded?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help children understand that their words and actions today are seeds — and that God's world is designed so that good seeds eventually produce a good harvest?
verses.do_it_today: Speak one genuinely kind word and do one genuinely good deed today. Trust God to let them bear fruit.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child's kind words flowing out as a stream of flowers and fruit, and their working hands receiving a harvest basket in return, warm watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The way of a fool is right in his own eyes: but he that hearkeneth unto counsel is wise.
verses.little_bible: A fool always thinks they are right. But the wise person listens to good advice. Wise people do not think they know everything.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wise people listen to good advice.
verses.meaning: The fool's defining characteristic is self-certainty — they are always right in their own estimation, closed to outside perspective. Wisdom, by contrast, is self-aware enough to know its own limits and humble enough to receive counsel.
verses.prayer: God, help me listen to wise counsel, not just myself.
verses.discussion_question: Do you find it easy or hard to listen to advice? Why?
verses.family_discussion: How do we model openness to counsel in front of our children — showing them that even adults need wisdom from others and from God?
verses.do_it_today: Ask one trusted adult for advice about something you are facing today. Then really listen — don't just wait to disagree.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child sitting attentively while an elder shares wise words, the child leaning in with an open expression, warm soft watercolour scene

verses.kjv: A fool's wrath is presently known: but a prudent man covereth shame.
verses.little_bible: A fool loses their temper right away. Everyone can see it! But a wise person stays calm. They do not show every bad feeling.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wise people stay calm. Fools show their anger fast.
verses.meaning: The fool is emotionally reactive — anger immediately visible and out of control. The prudent person practises self-restraint: not suppressing what is real, but managing how and when it is expressed. Wisdom governs emotion rather than being governed by it.
verses.prayer: God, help me stay calm when I am angry.
verses.discussion_question: What helps you stay calm when you feel really angry?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach children to process strong emotions without explosive reactions — building the kind of emotional wisdom the proverb describes?
verses.do_it_today: The next time you feel angry today, count to five silently before you react. Notice whether that helps.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child calmly and quietly managing their feelings while another child reacts in a temper tantrum, peaceful vs stormy contrast, gentle watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: An honest witness delivereth true things: but a false witness deceit.
verses.little_bible: An honest witness tells the truth. A false witness tells lies. Truth delivers; lies deceive.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Honest witnesses tell only the truth.
verses.meaning: The courtroom image extends to all of life: how we report on what we have seen, what we say about others, whether we can be trusted as a source of truth. The honest witness delivers reality; the false witness delivers deception that harms the innocent.
verses.prayer: God, help me always be an honest witness.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it so important to tell the truth about what you saw?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help children understand that truthful testimony — whether in formal settings or in everyday family life — is a matter of justice and love for neighbour?
verses.do_it_today: If someone asks what happened today, tell the whole truth — even if a little part is embarrassing. Practice being a true witness.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child standing up straight and speaking clearly with a glow of truth around them, versus a shadowy figure whispering deception, watercolour contrast

verses.kjv: There is that speaketh like the piercings of a sword: but the tongue of the wise is health.
verses.little_bible: Some words cut like a sharp sword — they hurt deeply. But the wise person's words are like medicine — they bring healing.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wise words heal. Cruel words cut like swords.
verses.meaning: Words have the power to wound as severely as a physical weapon — or to heal as powerfully as medicine. The image is visceral and real: careless, cruel, or cutting speech causes genuine damage. Wise speech actively promotes health and wholeness.
verses.prayer: God, make my words bring healing, not hurt.
verses.discussion_question: Have you ever been healed or hurt by someone's words?
verses.family_discussion: What does our family's everyday speech feel like — more like a sword or more like medicine? Where do we most need to improve?
verses.do_it_today: Think of someone who has been hurt by harsh words. Speak one healing, kind word to them today.
verses.illustration_prompt: A sword and a medicine bottle side by side, one representing hurtful words and one healing words, rendered as a warm watercolour illustration with children watching

verses.kjv: The lip of truth shall be established for ever: but a lying tongue is but for a moment.
verses.little_bible: Truth lasts forever. Lies only last for a moment before they fall apart.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Truth lasts. Lies fade away quickly.
verses.meaning: Truth is permanent; lies are fragile and temporary. Even when a lie appears to succeed, it cannot be maintained forever. Truth, however, endures precisely because it is aligned with reality — and with God who is Truth.
verses.prayer: God, help me choose truth that lasts forever.
verses.discussion_question: Have you ever seen a lie fall apart? What happened?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help children understand the permanence of truth versus the inevitable collapse of deception — and why this makes honesty not just right but wise?
verses.do_it_today: Think of one area where you have been stretching or avoiding the truth. Choose truth there today — even if it is hard.
verses.illustration_prompt: A golden pillar of truth standing firm forever while a flimsy lying structure crumbles and fades away, luminous watercolour contrast illustration

verses.kjv: Deceit is in the heart of them that imagine evil: but to the counsellors of peace is joy.
verses.little_bible: The heart that plans evil is full of deceit. But those who work for peace — they are filled with joy.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Peacemakers are filled with joy.
verses.meaning: What fills the heart of those who plot evil is deceit — corruption at the core. By contrast, those who pursue peace — who bring reconciliation, calm, and harmony — experience genuine joy. The connection between inner purity and inner joy is direct.
verses.prayer: God, make me a joyful maker of peace.
verses.discussion_question: How does it feel when you help two friends stop fighting?
verses.family_discussion: Is our family one that makes peace or one that makes conflict? How do we cultivate a household that reflects the 'counsellors of peace' this proverb describes?
verses.do_it_today: If there is any conflict or tension in your relationships today, be the one who tries to bring peace. Notice the joy that follows.
verses.illustration_prompt: Two children who were arguing now smiling and shaking hands while a third child beams between them, warm joyful watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: There shall no evil happen to the just: but the wicked shall be filled with mischief.
verses.little_bible: No lasting evil falls on the just person. God protects them. But the wicked fill themselves with trouble.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: God protects the just from real evil.
verses.meaning: This is a promise grounded in God's sovereignty and care: ultimate evil — the kind that destroys forever — will not ultimately prevail over the just. Hardships may come, but God's protection is real. The wicked, however, accumulate trouble through their own choices.
verses.prayer: God, keep me just and under Your protection.
verses.discussion_question: How do you feel knowing God protects those who do right?
verses.family_discussion: How do we hold together the promise of God's ultimate protection of the righteous with the reality that just people do face hardship in this world?
verses.do_it_today: Thank God today for specific ways He has protected your family. Name them out loud together.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child surrounded by a gentle shield of divine light while storm clouds pass over them without touching them, peaceful watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Lying lips are abomination to the LORD: but they that deal truly are his delight.
verses.little_bible: God hates lying lips — they are disgusting to Him. But people who deal truly are His delight. God loves honest people.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: God hates lying. God loves honesty.
verses.meaning: The language here is among the strongest in Proverbs: lying is an 'abomination' — a word of intense divine revulsion. Conversely, truthful dealing produces divine 'delight' — God's pleasure and joy. This verse makes honesty a matter of God's character and nature, not merely social utility.
verses.prayer: God, let my lips be Your delight, not Your disgust.
verses.discussion_question: Why does God feel so strongly about lying?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate in our children a deep sense that lying is not just 'getting in trouble with parents' but a matter of grieving God — and that truthfulness is a way of delighting the LORD?
verses.do_it_today: Every time you speak today, ask: 'Is this true?' Make honest speech a deliberate, conscious act.
verses.illustration_prompt: A bright glowing face representing God's delight over a truthful child, contrasted with a dark shadow over a lying mouth, watercolour concept illustration

verses.kjv: A prudent man concealeth knowledge: but the heart of fools proclaimeth foolishness.
verses.little_bible: A wise person does not show off everything they know. But fools shout out their foolishness for everyone to hear.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wise people do not show off their knowledge.
verses.meaning: Wisdom knows when to speak and when to be silent. The prudent person does not display all their knowledge — they hold back, discern the moment, and speak when appropriate. The fool, by contrast, cannot contain their emptiness and broadcasts it freely.
verses.prayer: God, help me be wise about when to speak.
verses.discussion_question: Is it always good to say everything you know?
verses.family_discussion: How do we model and teach the discipline of timely speech — knowing when to hold back and when to share what we know?
verses.do_it_today: Practice holding back one thought today that you would normally blurt out. Wait and see if the right moment comes to share it wisely.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child sitting quietly and listening while another child loudly announces everything they know to an uninterested crowd, gentle watercolour contrast

verses.kjv: The hand of the diligent shall bear rule: but the slothful shall be under tribute.
verses.little_bible: The hard worker rises to lead. The lazy person ends up serving others — always under someone else's control.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Hard workers rise to lead. Lazy people fall behind.
verses.meaning: Diligence produces leadership and authority; laziness produces subjugation and dependency. This is not about power for its own sake but about the natural outcome of character: those who work hard and faithfully are trusted with greater responsibility.
verses.prayer: God, help me work hard and grow in responsibility.
verses.discussion_question: Have you ever been given more responsibility because you worked hard?
verses.family_discussion: How are we progressively giving our children more responsibility as they show diligence — building the experience of earning trust through faithful work?
verses.do_it_today: Do your chores or school work today with full effort. Don't do the minimum — do your best and see what follows.
verses.illustration_prompt: A diligent child standing confidently as a leader while peers look on with admiration, compared to a lazy child sitting idle, warm achievement watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Heaviness in the heart of man maketh it stoop: but a good word maketh it glad.
verses.little_bible: A heavy, sad heart makes a person droop and stoop. But one good word can lift them up and make them glad.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: One good word can make a sad heart glad.
verses.meaning: Anxiety and grief weigh the human spirit down — visibly, physically. But a word of encouragement, care, or comfort has remarkable power to lift the heaviness. We are made for encouraging speech, and the impact of a single good word is never trivial.
verses.prayer: God, help me speak words that lift people up.
verses.discussion_question: Who needs a good word from you today?
verses.family_discussion: Do we notice the heaviness in each other's hearts in our family — and do we reach for an encouraging word rather than silence or criticism?
verses.do_it_today: Find someone who looks heavy or discouraged today. Say one genuinely good, warm word to them. Watch what happens.
verses.illustration_prompt: A drooping, sad child being lifted up and made to smile by a kind friend speaking a good word, warm gentle watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: The righteous is more excellent than his neighbour: but the way of the wicked seduceth them.
verses.little_bible: The righteous person stands out above others. But the wicked person's path leads them astray. They do not even know it.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Righteousness makes you stand out for good.
verses.meaning: The righteous person serves as a model and a guide — their excellence is for the benefit of those around them. The wicked are seduced by their own path — drawn further into error without realising it, led astray by the very way they have chosen.
verses.prayer: God, help me be a good example.
verses.discussion_question: Can you be a good example to the people around you this week?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help children understand that righteousness is not just personal — it has a positive effect on all those around us, making us 'more excellent' in the sense of being a blessing to neighbours?
verses.do_it_today: Do one thing today that sets a good example for someone watching you — a sibling, classmate, or friend.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child shining brightly as a guide among friends who look to them, a righteous light leading others on the right path, gentle watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The slothful man roasteth not that which he took in hunting: but the substance of a diligent man is precious.
verses.little_bible: The lazy person does not even cook what they caught. They waste what they have! But the diligent person's things are precious because they are well cared for.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Lazy people waste what they have. Diligent people treasure it.
verses.meaning: Laziness is not just about failing to start — it includes failing to finish, failing to complete the cycle of labour. The slothful person even abandons their gains. The diligent person, by contrast, tends and values what they have, making their substance precious.
verses.prayer: God, help me finish what I start and not waste.
verses.discussion_question: Have you ever started something and never finished it?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate follow-through and completion in our children — helping them understand that finishing well is as important as starting well?
verses.do_it_today: Finish one thing today that you have left incomplete. All the way to the end — then put it away properly.
verses.illustration_prompt: A lazy child sitting next to an uncoooked meal while a diligent child carefully prepares and enjoys their food, warm kitchen watercolour contrast

verses.kjv: In the way of righteousness is life; and in the pathway thereof there is no death.
verses.little_bible: The righteous path leads to life. On that path, there is no death. Walk right and live forever.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The righteous path leads to life, not death.
verses.meaning: This closing verse is a magnificent promise and a fitting summary of the chapter. Righteousness is not a burdensome set of rules but a living path — and that path leads to life itself. The pathway of righteousness is the pathway to life with God, both now and eternally. Death has no final claim on those who walk in His way.
verses.prayer: God, keep me on the righteous path that leads to life.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean that righteousness leads to life, not death?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that righteousness is not merely about avoiding punishment, but about finding the path to true and eternal life — the life God designed us to live?
verses.do_it_today: Write or say the memory verse together as a family: 'In the way of righteousness is life.' Let it be your declaration for the week.
